sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Urban Electric Cargo Bicycles and Step-Through Scooters

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa-New Zealand Double Taxation Relief Agreement (2002)
Sino-Samoa Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (2018)
Samoa-Germany Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (1993)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2007 (as amended in 2017); Companies Act 2001 (Part XX through s.197); International Companies Amendment Act 2019 (beneficial ownership registers); Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime (Amendment) Act 2008; Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Prevention Regulations 2020.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of constitutional documents (Memorandum and Articles of Association) for the offshore entity, if executed abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (Samoa acceded effective 2019); consular legalization is required only for non-apostille countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent government authority in the holder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (for countries not party to the Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and professional reference letter for each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution and licensed professional legal/accounting firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille or notarization required, but issuer must be current and signed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or equivalent) for existing corporate entities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the company's country of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, United Kingdom OFSI sanctions, and the Samoa Terrorist Designation List published under the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU). Enhanced due diligence is triggered for any PEP, PEP-relative, or close associate under the FATF 75 recommended risk factors; ongoing transaction monitoring and annual user due diligence refresh are required for all internal files.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – online name search and reservation portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be rendered in Latin alphabetic characters. English and Samoan orthography are accepted; scripts such as Chinese, Cyrillic, or Arabic are not permitted in the registered name. If the name is in a foreign language (non-Samoan), a transliterated Latin-script version of at least 60% of the primary commercial identifier must be filed simultaneously.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Company (unless used in its full name)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An initial name reservation is valid for 30 days and may be renewed for one further 30-day period upon payment of a renewal fee. If a name is rejected or regarded as undesirable under s.18 of the International Companies Act 1987, the applicant may submit a written appeal to the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice. The Registrar must determine the appeal within 14 days. If dissatisfied, the applicant may file a further appeal with the Minister of Commerce within 21 days of the Registrar's decision. No judicial review is sought before exhausting the administrative appeal, but the Supreme Court may be petitioned if the right of appeal is denied.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are permitted in the sense that the registered office must be a physical address in Samoa maintained by the licensed registered agent, but the company may conduct all operational activities abroad. Online conference rooms and virtual reception facilities are acceptable for client meetings, provided the legal registered office is maintained at the registered agent's street address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for an industrial micro-mobility OEM in the Standard Low Risk tier is approximately 2.8% (based on FIU/SIFA annual sampling and RCA inspection ratio for international companies with no local real estate operations). The presence of a physical registered office and the absence of in-country premises will not increase inspection frequency unless suspicious activity is flagged.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation fee (International Companies Registry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the International Companies (Fees) Regulations 2012

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation filing fee (International Company registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per the International Companies (Fees) Regulations 2012 (based on WST 300 equivalent at 0.38 rate)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent fee - annual compliance and registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered agent (licensed under the International Companies Act)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark in Apia; includes registered office, agent services, and standard UBO register maintenance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register preparation and filing (initial filing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee for beneficial ownership register compilation and submission to the central register

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance consultant or licensed agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-head transaction screening benchmark (5 individuals x USD 32)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille of corporate resolutions and passport copies (offshore documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in origin country + apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: International standard notary and apostille fees; average for three sets of documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of Good Standing / company extract for corporate shareholder (if applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Original jurisdiction registry fees and apostille
One-time client onboarding, KYC, and customer due diligence file set-up

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987, as amended (Nos. 32 of 1987, 15 of 1993, 8 of 1998, 22 of 2008), sections 4 (incorporation by registration), 7 (application for incorporation), 8 (certificate of incorporation), 12 (memorandum and articles), 27 (registered office and registered agent), 63 (directors); read with the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2021 and the International Companies (Fees) Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia; applications filed exclusively through a licensed registered agent approved by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 Application for Incorporation together with the subscribed Memorandum and Articles of Association; the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum authorised or paid-up capital; the Company may adopt a nominal capital of one or more shares of no par value under section 13 of the International Companies Act 1987. No escrow or bank deposit of paid-up capital is required, but the subscription price for issued shares must be fully paid and recorded in the register of members, and the controller must maintain working capital sufficient for the intended electric cargo e-bike manufacturing operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the subscription of 10,000 ordinary shares by the initial subscriber is accepted and, upon payment, those shares are allotted and issued; the subscriber is entered in the register of members. (2) The registered office maintained by the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, is adopted as the Company's statutory registered office for all purposes under the International Companies Act 1987. (3) [Name] is appointed director and [Name] is appointed company secretary, each to serve until previously removed or resigned. (4) The officers and registered agent are authorised to open bank accounts, execute agreements, and file all instruments to give effect to this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), via SIFA-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search and reservation request through a SIFA-licensed registered agent. The proposed name must end with 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated' or an approved abbreviation, must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, and must not imply any prohibited government or banking activity. The agent files the reservation form and receives a Name Approval Certificate.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copy of the ultimate beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the agent submits an alternative name within 2 business days or lodges a written appeal with the Registrar for a binding determination; no additional government fee is charged for one resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered agent and notary public or Commissioner of Oaths in Samoa; acceptance by the Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles in English containing the name clause, registered office clause, object clause, authorised share capital clause and director/secretary provisions. The initial subscriber executes the constitutional documents in counter-parts before a notary public or a licensed agent officer. Each proposed director signs the Consent to Act as Director form.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (subscribed and witnessed)
Consent to act as director (signed by each director)
Consent to act as company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defective or non-compliant clause is corrected by a deed of rectification executed by the subscriber before submission; if discovered after incorporation, the Articles are amended by a special resolution of members and refiled with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of SIFA-Licensed Registered Agent and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appoint a SIFA-licensed registered agent whose approved office in Apia, Samoa serves as the Company's statutory registered office. The agent executes the acceptance and registered office declaration and holds the Company's seal, statutory registers and share certificates in custody, in compliance with section 27 of the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Copy of the agent's SIFA licence
Agent's client due diligence file for the beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar objects to the nominated agent or office, an alternative SIFA-licensed agent is substituted promptly; the original submission date can be preserved by a Registrar's discretionary waiver where no bad faith is shown.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Application for Incorporation and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 28 days of name approval, the licensed agent files Form 1 Application for Incorporation with the statutory attachments through the MCIL/SIFA lodgment window and pays the USD 100 government fee plus the agent's professional disbursement. The Registrar conducts a completeness and legality review within the prescribed service period.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (certified copy)
Beneficial ownership declaration under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2021
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a Notice of Defect is issued, the agent rectifies the deficiencies within 14 days and resubmits; if the defect is incurable, the application may be withdrawn and refiled, and the original government fee is credited against the new application within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Kit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the application, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, and the International Company becomes a body corporate from the date stated on the certificate. The registered agent assembles the corporate kit comprising the certificate, share certificates, common seal, minute book, share register, register of directors and register of charges.
required_dossiers: Extract from the Register of International Companies
Common seal (rubber or metal) in the Company's name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains typographical or substantive errors, the agent files a written request for a certificate of correction; the Registrar issues an amended certificate with the original effective date within 3 business days at no additional fee for Registrar error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Officer Appointment and Post-Incorporation Statutory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; registered agent; Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the statutory first board meeting (electronically if the Articles so permit) to pass the First Board Resolution, approve the issue of shares, adopt the registers, ratify the registered office, appoint the company secretary, and authorise the opening of corporate bank accounts. The agent then files any required post-incorporation notices, such as the beneficial ownership return and the register of directors, and prepares the AEOI/RECS reporting profile with the Ministry of Revenue.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a post-incorporation filing is rejected for a formal defect, the agent corrects the schedule and refiles without penalty when the delay is attributable to the Registry or AEOI system and does not exceed 30 days; late filing penalties otherwise apply under the International Companies Act 1987.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa Investment Promotion Corporation (SIPC) and Foreign Investment Division, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Foreign Investment Certificate (FIC) under the Foreign Investment Act 2000, together with a Manufacturing Business Licence issued by the MCIL Business Registry and a Development Consent under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004; the International Company's tax-exempt offshore status does not exempt the physical factory from these local operational approvals.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Initial Environmental Examination (IEE) required for e-bike assembly, metal fabrication, powder coating and lithium-ion battery pack assembly; upgraded to a Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) where annual production exceeds 10,000 units, where solvent or VOC usage exceeds the prescribed threshold, or where the site is located in a coastal, water-catchment or environmentally sensitive zone under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero untreated industrial wastewater discharge; any pre-treated discharge must comply with pH 6.5-9.0, TSS below 50 mg/L, oil and grease below 10 mg/L, and biochemical oxygen demand below 30 mg/L; VOC emissions from painting and coating lines must achieve at least 90% abatement efficiency or a stack concentration below 20 ppm; battery scrap, e-waste and hazardous waste must be segregated in sealed authorised containers and transported only by MNRE-licensed waste carriers under the Waste Management Act and Water Resources Management Act 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) before factory occupation; structural load clearance and building permit from the Buildings Management Division, Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI); and workplace registration and occupational safety and health clearance from the Labour Division, MCIL under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013, including emergency evacuation plans, fire warden training, hazardous substance storage approval, machine guarding and lifting equipment inspection for the assembly lines.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Ministry of Revenue (MoR), Apia, Samoa – official taxpayer portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws; customs administration: Samoa Customs Service (Ministry for Revenue) operating ASYCUDA World.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company (IC) formed under the International Companies Act 2016 must first be incorporated through a licensed SIFA (Samoa International Finance Authority) registration agent. Following incorporation, the IC files a Ministry of Revenue 'Non-Resident Taxpayer Registration / TIN Application' (Form TIN-NR-01) accompanied by: (1) Certificate of Incorporation; (2) Registered Office Certificate; (3) Licensed Agent Consent; (4) Beneficial Ownership Declaration; and (5) Tax Exemption Certificate application. The MoR issues the Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) within 5 business days. The Tax Exemption Certificate is issued by MoR concurrently with the IC annual license renewal, confirming exemption from income tax, withholding tax, stamp duty, capital gains tax, and exchange control on all offshore business activities. No minimum capital or physical Samoan office is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone – An International Company under the International Companies Act 2016 is statutorily treated as a non-resident corporation and is exempt from all Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, dividend/interest/royalty withholding tax, gift and estate duties, and stamp duty on its worldwide offshore income and transactions. Tax exemption is automatic upon issuance of the Tax Exemption Certificate; the IC becomes taxable only if it carries on prescribed domestic trading activity in Samoa with residents, in which case the Income Tax Act 2015 applies to Samoan-source income only. Manufacturing and export of electric cargo e-bikes to non-resident customers falls wholly within the tax-exempt zone and incurs 0% corporate income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box transparent entity election exists under Samoan law. However, an IC may file with the MoR a 'Hybrid Entity Consistency Declaration' under the Income Tax Act 2015 to align Samoa's opaque entity classification with a counterpart jurisdiction's check-the-box transparent treatment, thereby addressing hybrid mismatch outcomes under BEPS Actions 2. An IC may also elect to apply for a 'Domestic Activity Permit' from SIFA/MoR to carry on an approved local support service (e.g., warehousing, after-sales servicing) with a Samoan subsidiary; such an election subjects only the domestic activity to VAGST and income tax while preserving the exempt offshore manufacturing and export status. Any election is valid for the tax year and must be filed at least 30 days before year-end.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST – Value Added Goods and Services Tax (Samoa VAGST Act 2008, as amended by the VAGST (Amendment) Act 2017), administered by the Samoa Ministry of Revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT$ 100,000 (Samoan Tālā) cumulative annual taxable turnover threshold for mandatory VAGST registration; voluntary registration is permitted where annual turnover exceeds SAT$ 60,000. An exporting IC that exclusively zero-rates its e-bike export turnover may nevertheless be required to register and file monthly VAGST returns solely to claim input credits on domestic raw materials, components, logistics, utilities, and agency fees.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAGST-registered exporters must issue sequentially numbered electronic tax invoices through the MoR Taxpayer E-Services Portal (e-Invoicing module). Each export invoice above SAT$ 100 must be submitted digitally at the time of issuance; the MoR system performs near-real-time validation of the TIN, invoice sequence, tax category (zero-rated export), and buyer residency, returning an 18-digit Digital Fiscal Clearance Reference (DFCR) that must be printed on the final invoice and customs export declaration. No physical fiscal stamping machine is required, but the exporter's ERP/accounting system must be capable of API-based invoice transmission to the MoR gateway (SOAP/REST), and all invoice data must be hosted in or accessible to Samoa for 7 years. Failure to obtain a DFCR renders the invoice non-deductible for the buyer and disqualifies the corresponding input credit claim for the exporter.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the physical export of goods (including electric cargo e-bikes, spare parts, and accessory kits) provided that: (a) the goods are exported by a VAGST-registered person within 60 days of the tax invoice date; (b) title in the goods passes to a non-resident buyer; (c) the goods leave Samoa and are delivered to a destination outside Samoa; (d) the exporter retains prescribed export evidence; and (e) the exporter holds a valid Tax Exemption Certificate (for ICs). Direct services ancillary to the exported goods (design, integration, OEM after-sales remote diagnostics) that are performed in Samoa and enjoyed outside Samoa are likewise zero-rated; support services consumed in Samoa are taxable at 15%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoa Customs CED-01, lodged through ASYCUDA World)
Commercial invoice stamped with the MoR Digital Fiscal Clearance Reference (DFCR)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing the goods departed Samoa and delivered to the non-resident buyer
Packing list and certificate of origin (Samoa Chamber of Commerce)
Vendor/OEM sales contract or purchase order identifying the non-resident buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a licensed Samoan commercial bank evidencing receipt of foreign currency payment
Certificate of non-residency of the buyer (supporting evidence such as foreign TIN or certificate of incorporation)
Freight forwarding agent's export certificate of receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Samoa Ministry of Revenue may reopen a zero-rated supply within 4 years of the relevant VAGST return. If export documentation or the DFCR cannot be substantiated, the full 15% VAGST is assessed retrospectively together with monthly default interest of 2% on the unpaid tax. Deliberate or fraudulent zero-rating claims attract a civil penalty of 200% of the evaded tax, a criminal fine not exceeding SAT$100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 3 years under section 78 of the VAGST Act 2008. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the 180-day deadline constitutes a breach of Samoa's Exchange Control Regulations 2005, rendering the exporter liable to forfeiture of up to 50% of the unrepatriated amount and suspension of VAGST refund privileges; however, a Certified International Company holding a valid Tax Exemption Certificate is wholly exempt from exchange control and may retain or repatriate proceeds offshore at its discretion. Exporters are also exposed to clawback of all input VAGST credits previously allowed on materials attributable to the non-exported or mischaracterized supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) — Falefa o Tupe Tutotonu o Samoa, operating under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984 and the Exchange Control Act 1978
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa operates a managed float for the Samoan Tala (WST) with broad convertibility on the current account, including trade transactions and normal remittances, subject to submission of supporting documentation to authorized dealer banks. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment inflows, profit repatriation, and offshore loan disbursements, require CBS general or specific approval under the Exchange Control Act. Profit remittance by non-resident shareholders of an International Company is generally permitted once the company is tax-exempt and provides a certificate of compliance from the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), but the remittance is subject to a final withholding tax of 10% on dividends unless an applicable tax treaty reduces this. Practical hurdles include the need to present audited financial statements, board resolutions declaring the dividend, and confirmation that no domestic tax liabilities are outstanding. The CBS imposes real-time reporting thresholds on all cross-border wire transfers, and funds may be temporarily held pending verification of economic substance or beneficial ownership information.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations, all export proceeds must be repatriated to Samoa within 90 calendar days of shipment date. Once received in an authorized dealer bank account, the proceeds must be converted to WST at the prevailing market rate within one business day unless the exporter obtains a specific CBS exemption to retain the balance in foreign currency for verified commercial working capital. Exemptions are granted only for recurring export receivables in the same foreign currency and require quarterly reporting to CBS. The mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 100% for non-exempt export receipts; no partial retention is permitted for ordinary export sales without prior written approval.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low to Medium for offshore digital EMIs. Samoan law does not license foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs) to hold WST-denominated accounts or to provide payment services to residents or registered international companies. An offshore EMI, such as a UK FCA-authorised e-money institution, may be used as a non-resident treasury vehicle for receiving pre-shipment deposits or invoicing in foreign currency, but it cannot clear funds into the local banking system without a corresponding Samoan dealer bank relationship. The CBS maintains strict anti-money laundering rules requiring all in-country payment services to be rendered by licensed commercial banks or licensed money remitters. Therefore, the offshore EMI route is legally permissible only for pre-funding of foreign currency raw material purchases, provided no WST conversion occurs, and all transactions are reported to the CBS via the beneficiary bank. Any attempt to use an EMI for recurring operational disbursements to Samoan suppliers would be non-compliant.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Samoa's anti-money laundering regulations under the Financial Institutions Act 1996 and the KYC Code issued by the Central Bank require that at least one authorized signatory who is a director or senior officer of the International Company must appear physically before a bank officer for the initial account opening interview. Remote opening is generally not permitted for foreign-owned International Companies unless an existing banking relationship of at least two years with the same bank is demonstrated, in which case the local branch manager may waive the physical appearance upon a notarized and apostilled certified copy of the director's passport being lodged and a video call interview conducted. For new customers, the mandate is strict: primary signatories, the ultimate beneficial owner(s) owning 25% or more, and the company secretary must be identified and verified through physical passport inspection. The board resolution appointing authorized signatories must be apostilled by the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, or certified by the Registrar of International Companies if the resolution was executed outside Samoa.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mixed or opaque beneficial ownership structure involving a trust or nominee shareholder
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal trust deed or nominee declaration, a complete chain of ownership diagram showing all natural persons as ultimate beneficial owners, certified copies of passports for all UBOs, a letter of comfort from the Samoan trustee or licensed nominee service provider, and a statement of source of wealth and source of funds signed by each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company status perceived as a potential money-laundering shell
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A valid International Company Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Samoa International Finance Authority, a copy of the filed annual return demonstrating economic substance or an exemption therefor, a detailed business plan describing the manufacture and export of electric cargo bicycles, evidence of physical office or warehouse presence in Samoa or a third-party service agreement, and financial projections supported by binding purchase orders from overseas buyers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume or unusual cross-border wire transfers inconsistent with low-risk manufacturing profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices, bills of lading, customs export declarations, supplier contracts for raw materials, banking confirmation of the underlying trade in micro-mobility OEM goods, a treasury management policy limiting per-transaction thresholds, and real-time reporting of all transfers to the Samoan Financial Intelligence Unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Director or UBO residency outside Samoa in a high-risk jurisdiction (e.g., jurisdiction with FATF monitoring)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of valid residence permits or visas from their country of residence, an independent background check from a reputable due diligence provider, evidence of legitimate employment or business ownership, and enhanced documentation of the origin of initial capital injection via a regulated financial institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for inbound capital injection: (1) The shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner wires funds from a personally held bank account in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction to the International Company's capital escrow or operational account at a licensed Samoan commercial bank. (2) The wire must contain a precise purpose code using the SWIFT MT103 field 70: 'INVCAP' (capital injection) or 'INVESTMENT EQUITY', and must reference the company registration number. (3) The Samoan bank will request a board resolution authorizing the issuance of shares or recording the shareholder loan, a statement of account from the remitting bank showing the source of funds, and a certified copy of the share register reflecting the increase in paid-up capital. (4) The bank is required to verify the identity of the remitter and the ultimate beneficiary; any split transfers below reporting thresholds to evade scrutiny are prohibited. (5) For capital injections exceeding USD 50,000 or equivalent, the Samoan bank must submit an ExPost report to the CBS within five business days; therefore, the documentation bundle must be assembled in advance. (6) If the funds are for a shareholder loan rather than equity, a loan agreement with commercial terms must be lodged, and the CBS may require prior approval for any non-resident borrowing exceeding WST 1,000,000.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) For supplier payments of raw materials and components, use SWIFT MT103 direct transfers from the Samoan operational account to the supplier's bank, with good instructions including the supplier's IBAN or account numbers, SWIFT/BIC codes, and precise purpose codes (e.g., 'TRADEPAY' for trade payment, 'PREPAY' for advance payment, or 'COMMLC' for documentary credit settlement). (2) For bulk or high-value settlements, a commercial letter of credit (L/C) issued by the Samoan bank in favor of the offshore supplier is acceptable; the L/C is typically irrevocable and confirmed by a prime international bank. Samoan banks require a margin or full collateralization for the L/C amount. (3) Disbursements for freight, insurance, and inspection fees can be settled via MT103 with supporting transport documents. (4) For larger transactions exceeding WST 200,000, the bank must verify the underlying trade document (invoice, packing list, and proof of shipment) before releasing funds, in order to comply with CBS exchange control rules. (5) Post-shipment export proceeds should be routed through the same Samoan bank to permit netting and reconciliation, but cross-currency netting with suppliers requires prior CBS approval unless the amounts are hedged via a licensed FX forward.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forward contracts with a licensed Samoan commercial bank, permitted only for hedging genuine commercial trade exposure and capped at a tenor of 12 months

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the Samoan Tala (WST) can be arranged offshore through non-resident banks, but only with prior CBS notice and subject to a demonstrated underlying trade exposure; settlement must be in a freely convertible currency

Cross-currency swaps (single or dual currency) with a licensed bank for the purpose of aligning working capital currency mismatches, subject to CBS approval for any swap involving WST, and limited to a maximum notional of the company's verified annual trade turnover
FX options (European style) purchased from a licensed dealer, used exclusively to protect minimum export revenue margins, with a maturity aligned to the underlying trade receivable cycle

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Declaration of Continued Compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation; filing is due on or before each annual registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of WST 100 (approximately US$35) per month or part thereof, up to a maximum WST 1,000 (approximately US$350); continued non-filing or non-payment for six consecutive months from the due date exposes the company to administrative strike-off and deregistration by the Registrar after publication of a gazetted strike-off notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership and AML/CFT Annual Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA) through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 31 days after the SIFSA-designated compliance period ending 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update the beneficial ownership register may result in regulatory fines up to WST 50,000 (approximately US$17,500), suspension or revocation of the registered agent's licence, and prohibition on the company making payments from its registered bank accounts; continued AML non-compliance can also trigger a SIFSA directive for administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory solely by virtue of International Company status. An independent audit becomes compulsory if the company's annual turnover exceeds WST 40 million (approximately US$14 million), total assets exceed WST 80 million (approximately US$28 million), the register of members exceeds 100 holders, or the shareholders by ordinary resolution require an audit. The Registrar may also require an audit where accounting records have not been properly maintained.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB; IFRS for SMEs is permitted on a voluntary basis for eligible International Companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a beneficial ownership register at the office of the licensed registered agent. Before each annual return date, the company must confirm and, if changed, update the particulars of senior managing officials, ultimate beneficial owners, and controllers. The registered agent conducts an annual risk-based UBO refresh using current nationality, tax identification, and source-of-funds declarations; a material change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the agent within 14 days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,000–$5,000 per year for a full IFRS audit if the threshold is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% under the Income Tax Act 2012; International Companies (ICs) classified in the Tax_Exempt_Zone pay 0% on qualifying offshore (international) income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Samoa International Company exemption: all foreign-source corporate income is exempt from Samoan income tax; no payroll tax on IC employees engaged offshore; no dividend withholding tax on IC distributions; the annual Registry Government Fee (calculated on share capital) substitutes for income tax; effective rate approximates 0% for a compliant pure offshore IC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Exempt IC status: no Samoan corporate income tax return is required; the recurring statutory filing is the International Company Annual Return filed with the Registrar of International Companies (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour). If the IC derives non-exempt Samoan-source domestic income, the Company Income Tax Return must be filed through the Samoa Ministry for Revenue Taxpayer Online Services portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (quarterly provisional tax installments apply only where non-exempt Samoan-source income is derived)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return due within 6 months after the income year-end: 30 June for the standard 31 December income year. Provisional installments, if triggered, fall due 31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Samoa TIN of the reporting entity; an IC should maintain an active TIN for banking and Swift LC/TT wire payment rail operations even while tax-exempt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the IC-in-Samoa TIN; a non-resident parent must not substitute its own foreign TIN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the 12-month assessment period; Samoa aligns with the calendar year unless an approved substituted accounting period exists.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm alignment with the parent group's fiscal year only if a formal substituted period was granted by the Ministry for Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report only Samoan-source assessable income. IC offshore turnover from e-cargo-bike OEM sales is excluded as exempt international income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule demonstrating that all revenue is foreign-source (offshore sales, foreign warehouses, no Samoan manufacturing footprint); a zero entry is acceptable only with that supporting schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim expenses strictly attributable to Samoan-source income; exempt foreign-source expenses must be excluded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not allocate group overhead from the non-resident parent against a nil Samoan tax base; double counting of exempt costs is a common audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply 25% to the net taxable amount in Box 4 after all allowable deductions and offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0 only where the full IC exemption applies; any positive entry must be paid with the return and reconciled to provisional installments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the assessed tax, minimum WST 200; late payment surcharge of 2% per month on the unpaid amount. Incorrect or false returns attract a penalty of up to WST 10,000 plus a 100% evasion penalty on the tax shortfall. For ICs, failure to pay Registry annual fees triggers late payment penalties and eventual strike-off from the International Companies Register.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory non-resident dividend withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 2012; reduced to 0% for distributions made by a Samoa International Company to non-resident shareholders under the International Companies Act 1987, provided the IC acts only as an IC and does not carry on domestic Samoan business.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where a shareholder claims a reduced DTA rate rather than the 0% IC exemption: (1) obtain a Samoa Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the Samoa Ministry for Revenue by filing Form TRC-1 together with the IC incorporation certificate, registered agent confirmation, and board resolution; (2) deliver the TRC and a signed DTA treaty relief declaration to the Samoan payor entity before dividend execution; (3) the payor retains the TRC and submits the DTA exemption schedule with its annual filing. Samoa's DTA network is limited (comprehensive agreements with Australia, New Zealand, and Turkey); each treaty must be examined individually for limitation-on-benefits and beneficial ownership clauses.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding tax on interest and royalties is 15% gross. DTA-reduced rates apply where a treaty is in force (beneficial owner conditions must be satisfied). Interest and royalties paid out by an exempt IC remain outside the Samoan WHT net where the payments relate to the IC's exempt offshore business; however, any royalty or interest charge connected with Samoan domestic-source activity is fully subject to the 15% statutory WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Samoa-specific threshold mandating Local File or Master File preparation is prescribed in the Income Tax Act 2012. The arm's length principle applies to all cross-border related-party transactions. Prudent compliance benchmark: maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation where annual cross-border related-party turnover exceeds WST 1,000,000 (approximately USD 370,000), covering purchases of e-bike components, royalties, management fees, and intercompany financing.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not maintain a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to BVI or Cayman. Nevertheless, the International Companies Act 1987 imposes mandatory presence requirements: a licensed registered agent and registered office in Samoa, a board of directors, and books and records maintained at the registered office. The IC tax-exempt zone status is contingent on deriving exclusively 'international income'; local manufacturing, local warehousing, or local sales activity in Samoa taints the exemption and converts the IC into an ordinary taxable resident company at 25%.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting actual manufacturing, assembly, or domestic sales of electric cargo e-bikes within Samoa while declaring all revenue as exempt offshore 'international income' to avoid the 25% corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Administration Act 2012: full reassessment of the tax shortfall, a 100% evasion penalty, 2% monthly late payment interest, and criminal fines up to WST 100,000 upon conviction; the Registrar may additionally revoke the IC status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly file or approve false returns are personally liable for the unpaid tax on a joint and several basis; prosecution may result in imprisonment of up to 5 years, asset freezes, and travel bans preventing departure from Samoa pending final assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC without a licensed registered agent or registered office in Samoa, failing to maintain board minutes or financial records in Samoa, or using nominee directors with no control over the e-bike OEM business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off from the International Companies Register, forfeiture of the tax-exempt status, retroactive assessment of 25% corporate income tax for the full period of non-compliance, and monetary penalties under the International Companies Act 1987.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be disqualified from holding Samoan corporate offices, prohibited from leaving Samoa, and held personally liable for the re-assessed corporate tax, interest, and penalty amounts where the sham structure was knowingly maintained.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using falsified invoices, inflated unit prices, or misleading Swift LC and TT wire payment descriptions in cross-border transactions for e-bike battery packs, motors, and components to shift profits to tax havens or obscure the ultimate beneficiary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007: fines up to WST 500,000 and/or imprisonment up to 10 years upon conviction; the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit must receive Suspicious Transaction Reports for any irregular trade-payment pattern; the underlying assets may be confiscated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior officers who knowingly direct trade-based money laundering face personal prosecution, imprisonment, personal fines, confiscation of personal assets, and travel restrictions; prior conviction does not preclude separate civil recovery proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring and paying dividends, royalties, or interest to non-resident shareholders without applying the 15% statutory withholding tax and without documented treaty relief (TRC and treaty declaration) or without satisfying the 0% IC exemption conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the full 15% withholding tax on the gross payment, 2% monthly late payment interest, late filing penalties, and a 100% false return penalty where the exemption was claimed without supporting documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors acting as withholding agents are personally liable for the unremitted WHT if they authorize distributions while aware of the non-compliance; criminal conviction carries fines and imprisonment of up to 3 years, with personal travel bans available to secure recovery.
